The sharp increase is driven by the war in the Middle East and disruptions to supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, one of the main routes for global oil and gas trade. Any restrictions or risks in this region immediately affect fuel and shipping costs.  The rise in fuel oil prices directly increases maritime shipping costs, which are eventually passed on to the prices of all goods, from electronics to food. This is essentially inflation that “sails” across the sea.  The market is already reacting. Carriers are raising rates, and businesses are beginning to reassess their supply chains. If the situation in the region does not stabilize, price increases could accelerate and hit the global economy harder than during the 2022 crisis, media reports say.

text: "Ran Goyili is not just a name, Ran is a son, a friend, a brave YSM fighter who on October 7 ran into the fire and defended with his body Kibbutz Alumim and the home of all of us. Ran fought like a hero and was kidnapped to Gaza. He is a symbol of supreme sacrifice, and thanks to him many of us are alive today." Hadassah, the sister of the late Shlomo Mansour, asked today at the Shabbat reception at the Kidnapped Square to connect two stories of heroism and death that were intertwined in one destiny: "Ran's relationship with us goes back one generation: Itzik, Ran's father, was in the Nahal nucleus in Kibbutz Kissuf, with my beloved brother, Shlomo Mansour. There, among the fields of the Negev, the two met. Itzik talks about Shlomo with praise and appreciation and with great respect, about a good, honest man, one who was always there for others.  My brother, Shlomo Mansour, was brutally kidnapped from his home in Kibbutz Kissuf on October 7 when he was 85 years old and taken handcuffed to his car and from there to Gaza. Those who knew Shlomo know that it is impossible to miss him - with the eternal smile, the light that radiated from him and the famous mustache that was his hallmark. After 513 long and tormented days Solomon was returned to us in a transaction and buried in the land of Kissuf.  The connection between Ran the warrior and Shlomo, the brother and guide, is the story of the beautiful and painful Land of Israel. This is a story about generations of builders and defenders who tied their fate in this land.  Ran continued the same line of values, the same commitment, the same silent statement "if needed, I'm here", and today we should be here for him.  And when we accept Shabbat, we will remember the strength of his spirit, his smile and the light of Ran and the shining smile of Shlomo.  Their light will continue to light our way." text: "Three and a half months ago I was in a completely different place, with no one to pick me up in moments of crisis, to laugh or cry with me, just alone." With these words, Ariel Konio opened his words this evening, at the last rally of Carmi Gat.   "Today I stand here together with my brother David, who returned with me from captivity, surrounded by so many amazing people. We both stand here as living proof that even in the face of the most terrible darkness, the human spirit can win." And David added and shared: "There were many nights when I didn't know if I would get to see daylight again, if I would hug my childhood again, if I would get to see them laugh, if I would ever return home. And here I am." David, Ariel and their family members thanked everyone who went out to the streets and squares to call for their release, to those who fought for them in the various sectors and to all those who did not stop, until the last abductee.
